Subject: Dedicated GPU capacity for Horizon Med — initial requirements

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this call last week. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize our expected workload so your team can recommend a SKU plan and a pilot configuration (we're aiming to buy Dedicated capacity if the pilot meets latency and cost targets).

Quick numbers:
- Peak steady concurrent requests: ~70 concurrent chat sessions (not just API calls, full chat state).
- Average request: 900 tokens in, 450 tokens generated (95th percentile generation length).
- Prompts have heavy context reuse — many sessions share a common patient-context prefix (60–80 tokens).
- Target latency: p95 <= 250 ms for short-turn responses (when response <150 tokens).
- Throughput requirement: at least 30 requests/sec sustained for batch windows.
- Model preference: we want to run an LLM ~70B param (customer prefers higher quality) but are open to quantized 8-bit or 4-bit variants.
- Regulatory: all inference must happen in US Dedicated — private networking, audit logs, and KMS for keys.

Attached is our Q1 usage report for baseline traffic. Could you propose initial SKU options (H100, A100, L4) and a recommended pilot: min capacity, target replicas, and risks we should be aware of? Also include rough monthly cost delta between options so our procurement can evaluate.

Thanks,
Alejandra

Alejandra — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. Below is a concise pilot recommendation and the tradeoffs we see for H100 / A100 / L4 given a 70B-class model with heavy context reuse. I kept the ask minimal so procurement can get a pilot approved quickly.

Executive recommendation (pilot):
- Pilot: 2-node Dedicated pool for 6 weeks, each node with 8x GPUs (choose the SKU per option below).
- Target: validate p95 latency on 150-token responses, steady 30 req/s aggregate, and confirm cache-hit benefits on shared prefixes.
- Canary routing: route 10% traffic to the Dedicated pool during pilot, fallback to hosted for overflow.

SKU tradeoffs (brief):
- H100 (best perf for large models):
  * Pros: Highest fp16/AMP throughput and excellent for large-context 70B models; strong memory bandwidth for activation-heavy workloads and KV cache; best latency headroom for p95 targets.
  * Cons: ~$X/month (premium), more power and cooling; fewer available SKUs in some regions.
- A100 (balanced):
  * Pros: Mature, predictable perf for 70B quantized variants; lower list price vs H100; broad availability.
  * Cons: Slightly higher p95 latency vs H100 for long-sequence generation; less memory bandwidth than H100 which can affect tail latency under heavy KV-cache pressure.
- L4 (inference-optimized, more efficient for smaller models):
  * Pros: Lowest cost and excellent for heavily quantized or distilled variants; lower power; good for throughput-focused workloads if model fits memory.
  * Cons: Limited if you want to run the full 70B float/low-quant degradation; may require model surgery or sharding and higher engineering effort.

Sizing notes and quick numbers (approx, Dev will follow up with bench numbers):
- Assumptions: 70 concurrent sessions active, ~450 tokens gen avg, batch windows tuned to preserve latency SLO. KV cache reuse expected to reduce compute for continued sessions by ~20–35%.
- H100 estimate: 8x H100 node can sustain ~40–50 concurrent high-quality streams at target latency when using Q4_0 or 8-bit with optimized kernels. So 2 nodes (16 GPUs) gives margin and supports pilot overhead.
- A100 estimate: 8x A100 node can sustain ~28–36 streams — firming up p95 requires additional replicas; pilot with 3 nodes (24 GPUs) would be more conservative.
- L4 estimate: if using a 4-bit quantized 70B distillation that fits in memory, an 8x L4 node can sustain ~30+ streams but quality risk is higher; recommend smaller pilot to validate quality.

Risks & mitigations:
- Memory pressure on full 70B (unquantized) will force model sharding across GPUs — increases latency and adds complexity. Mitigate by validating a 4-bit quantized build or a distilled 34B fallback.
- KV cache cold-starts: need to validate prefix caching and hot-shard placement; monitor cache hit rate closely.
- Procurement: H100 lead times can be longer — include a fallback plan to A100 for initial pilot.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev will run a quick benchmark (24–36h) across H100/A100/L4 variants with a sample of your Q1 workload.
2) We'll produce a one-page cost/coverage matrix and a pilot playbook (routing, canary, rollback).
3) If numbers look good, Redwood will provide a pilot SOW and DocuSign link for the pilot seat reservation.

Attaching a draft SKU estimate for quick procurement review.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Markus / Marissa — quick bench sketch and a couple of numbers you can drop into the one-pager. I'm copying the assumptions so procurement has context.

Bench assumptions (synthetic):
- Model: 70B-family, Q4_0 and Q8 variants tested; distill 34B for fallback.
- Input distribution: 60% short-turn (<150 tokens), 40% long-turn (>300 tokens).
- KV cache on shared prefixes yields 25% reduction in total FLOPs on average after warm-up.

Empirical numbers (approx):
- 8x H100 (PCIe or SXM): ~2200 tokens/sec aggregate decode for 450-token tails in optimized runtime; p95 latency headroom ~120–180 ms on short turns when batching is shallow.
- 8x A100: ~1500–1800 tokens/sec aggregate; p95 tail ~180–280 ms depending on batch mixing.
- 8x L4: ~1800–2100 tokens/sec for highly quantized 70B-distilled; however, model quality deltas observable on medical QA tasks.

Implications for pilot sizing:
- If Horizon prioritizes strict p95 latency and minimal model changes: H100 is the only SKU that consistently meets the 250 ms p95 with room to spare.
- If cost is highest priority and Horizon accepts a quantized/distilled model and additional QA: L4 can be compelling but requires a 2–3 week model rework and extra evals.
- A100 is the middle ground; good for initial rollouts if you accept a slightly higher safety buffer (we recommend +30% capacity).

Network / ops notes:
- KV cache co-location matters — schedule the same tenant pods to preserve locality and reduce PCIe hops on multi-GPU nodes.
- For pilot: enable prefix caching at route-level and keep eviction conservative (64–128MB per model shard).

I'll run a small suite on H100 and A100 overnight and attach results to the one-pager for Alejandra.
